title: Google's First-Time H-1B Visa Approvals Double as Company Pursues Global Staff Buyouts

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The number of new H-1B visa petitions granted to Google grew by 110% in the fiscal year ending Sept. 30, rising to 2,204 from 1,050 in the previous period. The surge in first-time approvals moved the company from No. 4 to No. 2 in the rank of employers receiving these visas, while across all employers, the total number of such petitions grew by roughly 11%.

The increase in specialized hiring occurs as Google manages its payroll amid heavy expenditures on artificial intelligence. The company has offered voluntary exit packages to staff in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland since June, with Swiss employees receiving up to one month of pay for every year worked, capped at 12 months. In the U.S., similar buyout waves occurred between January and February across the search, HR, and business divisions.

selectedTweets.text:
GOOGLE IS OFFERING EMPLOYEE BUYOUTS, AND ITS NEW H-1B APPROVALS JUST DOUBLED

Google confirmed to Reuters that since June it has offered voluntary exit packages to some staff in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland.

People familiar with the offer told Reuters the Swiss deal paid a month of salary per year worked, capped at 12 months.

In the US those offers have come in waves since January 2025, starting with the devices unit, then HR, then Search, then the business org this February.

In the fiscal year that ended Sept 30, USCIS approved 2,204 first-time H-1B petitions for Google, up from 1,050. 

That's 110% growth while all employers rose about 11%, and it moved Google from No. 4 to No. 2.
